# Twenty API review

Open-source (AGPL), API-first CRM: per-workspace generated REST + GraphQL APIs (core and metadata), 60-record batch calls with GraphQL batch upsert, HMAC-signed webhooks, a native MCP server, Cloud from $9/user/month or free self-hosted. Best for teams that want to own/self-host their CRM and still get REST, GraphQL, webhooks and MCP.

## Rate limits

Sources differ: the API page and import guide say 100 requests/minute and 60 records per batch call (~6,000 records/min, 600 ms between sustained calls, back off on 429); the pricing table says API calls 50/minute on Pro, 100/minute on Organization, custom on Enterprise.

Separately, apps get 500 requests/minute per application registration (shared by all installs) for requests made in the app's own name. Our hands-on calls returned no rate-limit headers. Plan on 50/min for Pro.

## How to get an API key

Twenty uses API key. The steps below follow Twenty's own docs.

1.  Create a Twenty account. API access starts on the Cloud Pro plan.
2.  Settings > Developers > API > + Create key: name, role (default Admin) and expiration (default Never); the key (a ~444-character JWT in our test) is shown once. Roles can be assigned under Settings > Members > Roles. OAuth for third-party apps
3.  Send it with every request: header: Authorization: Bearer <api\_key>.
4.  Make a first call: Create records (e.g. POST /rest/people, /rest/companies); REST and GraphQL both batch up to 60 records per request. Unique fields (People email, Companies domain) reject duplicates with 400. Keep the key in an environment variable, never in the command.
    
    ```
    curl -X POST "https://api.twenty.com/rest/{objectPlural}" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TWENTY_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{}'
    ```

## Strengths and limits

### Where it fits

-   Teams that want to own/self-host their CRM and still get REST, GraphQL, webhooks and MCP
-   Unique email (People) and domain (Companies) enforced at the database level, so API upserts cannot create duplicates
-   Unlimited custom objects and fields on every plan
-   Agent access via the workspace's own /mcp endpoint (OAuth 2.1 or API key)

### Where it falls short

-   High-volume syncs: 50 requests/minute on Cloud Pro (100 on Organization), 60 records per batch
-   Teams that need hundreds of pre-built integrations or a native HubSpot importer
-   Free cloud use: no free cloud plan; free only when self-hosted

### Worth knowing

-   Rate-limit sources conflict (docs 100/min vs pricing table 50/min on Pro). Sources: [docs.twenty.com/user-guide/data-migration/how-tos/import-data-via-api](https://docs.twenty.com/user-guide/data-migration/how-tos/import-data-via-api); [twenty.com/pricing](https://twenty.com/pricing)
-   Base URL: the docs give `https://api.twenty.com` (Cloud) and `https://{your-domain}` (self-host), with /rest, /graphql, /rest/metadata and /metadata as path prefixes; twenty.com/llms.txt gives `https://{workspace}.twenty.com/rest`. Our test: both api.twenty.com and onegtmlab.twenty.com returned the same data with the same key.
-   Soft-deleted records (UI: Command Menu > See deleted records) still count for uniqueness and are restored by a matching import. But a REST DELETE with an API key was a permanent delete in our test, so the domain was free immediately.
-   Contact auto-creation from email sync also creates companies from email domains (unique domain prevents duplicates, but junk companies are possible). Source: docs.twenty.com user-guide calendar-emails overview
-   Webhooks are created in the UI (Settings > Developers > Webhooks), fire on every create/update/delete of every object (no event filtering yet), and are signed. The inbound workflow webhook trigger is a unique URL; its setup page documents no authentication, so treat the URL as the secret or call the REST API with a key. Sources: [docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/webhooks](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/webhooks); [docs.twenty.com/user-guide/workflows/how-tos/connect-to-other-tools/set-up-a-webhook-trigger](https://docs.twenty.com/user-guide/workflows/how-tos/connect-to-other-tools/set-up-a-webhook-trigger)

4 moreShow fewer

-   Batch-size sources differ: the API page and import guide say up to 60 records per call; the Apps good-practices page's example is 'a createMany with upsert: true carrying 200 records is one request' with a 500 requests/minute per-app budget. Test the real cap. Sources: [docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/api](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/api); [docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/getting-started/good-practices](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/getting-started/good-practices)
-   Companies' domain is the composite field domainName.primaryLinkUrl in the API payload, not a flat 'domain'.
-   Trial: without a card the cloud trial is 7 days of Pro; the 30-day trial advertised on the pricing page needs a card in-app.
-   Integrations: Zapier is listed as a native connection method; Make and n8n are named only as no-code tools that reach Twenty through webhooks and the API (no native app verified). Sources: [docs.twenty.com/getting-started/core-concepts/calendar-and-email](https://docs.twenty.com/getting-started/core-concepts/calendar-and-email); [docs.twenty.com/llms-full.txt](https://docs.twenty.com/llms-full.txt) (webhook trigger guide)

### Our take

We evaluated Twenty as a CRM for our own team: in our comparison of free CRMs, the self-hosted edition, free with all Pro features, was the fallback after Attio. What we value is that unique emails on people and unique domains on companies are enforced at database level, since duplicate-free records are a hard requirement for us.

## Who should use it

Use Twenty for

Teams that want to own/self-host their CRM and still get REST, GraphQL, webhooks and MCP

Look elsewhere for

High-volume syncs: 50 requests/minute on Cloud Pro (100 on Organization), 60 records per batch

## Before you build

Four things to settle first, each read off Twenty's own pages.

-   **Confirm the API is on your plan**API access starts on the Cloud Pro plan. Free tier: Self-hosted Free: $0 with all Pro features (community support).
    
-   **Keep the key out of your code**API key. It is sent as: header: Authorization: Bearer <api\_key>.
    
-   **Design around the rate limit**Sources differ: the API page and import guide say 100 requests/minute and 60 records per batch call (~6,000 records/min, 600 ms between sustained calls, back off on 429); the pricing table says API calls 50/minute on Pro, 100/minute on Organization, custom on Enterprise.
    
-   **Know the catch before you scale**Rate-limit sources conflict (docs 100/min vs pricing table 50/min on Pro). Sources: [docs.twenty.com/user-guide/data-migration/how-tos/import-data-via-api](https://docs.twenty.com/user-guide/data-migration/how-tos/import-data-via-api); [twenty.com/pricing](https://twenty.com/pricing)
